oneLine: Grouping requests turns one expensive read into many cheap answers.
summary: At small batch sizes the server waits on memory, so serving requests together is nearly free (see 9.1.1). The gain stops once compute becomes the limit (see 9.1.2).

mechanism.title: Read once
mechanism.body: Each step streams the weights through the chip one time.

mechanism.title: Share it
mechanism.body: Every request in the group reuses that single stream.

mechanism.title: Hit the ceiling
mechanism.body: Eventually arithmetic, not memory, sets the pace.

callout.name: The bus rule
callout.body: A bus costs about the same to drive with one rider or forty.

figureRefs.lookFor: Where step time stops staying flat.

keyCards.label: Bound
keyCards.title: Memory first
keyCards.body: Small groups wait on memory, not maths.

keyCards.label: Lever
keyCards.title: Group size
keyCards.body: The main knob on throughput per chip.

workedExample.title: Cost per request
workedExample.setup: One read costs 16 ms whatever the group size, up to 16 requests.

conclusion.text: Going from 1 to 8 requests cuts the cost per request eightfold.

checkQuestion.explanation: The shared read is the expensive part, so sharing it is what helps.
checkQuestion.sourceQuote: A decode step reads every weight once, whatever the batch size.
checkQuestion.prompt: Fixture sum 0: one read costs 16 ms and serves 8 requests. Cost per request?
checkQuestion.methodHint: Divide the cost of the read by the requests sharing it.

reflect.prompt: Explain why a bigger group barely changes step time at first.
reflect.modelAnswer: The step is dominated by streaming the weights, and that stream is shared by every request in the group.
points: The weights are streamed once per step
Compute sits idle at a group of one
